    {
      "explanation":"household",
      "likelihood":"high",
      "reasoning":"A shared home address plausibly explains the address linkage, and the passed id_check establishes possession of the payment credentials and account identity. The recent home registration prevents the formal household exception but does not disprove this explanation."
    },
    {
      "explanation":"synthetic_identity",
      "likelihood":"low",
      "reasoning":"The newly opened account and shared destination could initially suggest coordinated identities. However, the passed identity and issuer authentication check resolves the required verification, and the packet provides no settling fraud outcome."

  "disposition":"clear",
  "citations":["R08","FP-2 §6.4(b)","FP-2 §6.3","FP-2 §6.6(b)","FP-2 §5.2","FP-2 §5.3(a)","FP-2 §8.1"],
  "next_check":"none",
  "memo":"R08 is the sole condition met, establishing Linkage. The home-address household exception does not apply because registration is too recent. No earlier outcome settles the order. Linkage requires id_check, which passed; all required verification is therefore complete. Under FP-2 §5.3(a), clear is mandatory and further adverse action is prohibited. Household sharing is the strongest benign explanation, while coordinated synthetic identities are less plausible after successful verification. No installments were due, so non-payment cannot support an adverse recommendation. No further check is needed."
